newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Matrix to raise A$48.6 mln in 1-for-2 issue.
newsitem.headline: Matrix to raise A$48.6 mln in 1-for-2 issue.

text.p: Australian paging group Matrix Telecommunications Ltd said it would raise A$48.6 million through a one-for-two renounceable right issue at A$0.80 a share.

Matrix said the rights issue will be fully underwritten by PBL Marketing Pty Ltd, a subsidiary of Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, Hellman & Friedman Asia Pacific III BV and investment group Innerhadden Ltd and associates in proportion to their interests in the company.
PBL Marketing and Hellman & Friedman own 29.5 percent and and 29.2 percent of the shares of Matrix respectively and have indicated to the company that they intend to take up their rights, it said.
The issue price compares with Monday's closing price of A$0.94, up nine cents from Friday's close of A$0.85.

"This fundraising will provide Matrix with funds to further develop its existing paging operations in Thailand, the Philippines, India and Indonesia and to pursue investment opportunities in telecommunications services in Asia which build on the company's existing infrastructure," president and chief executive officer Joe Yang said in a statement.

Matrix said its results for the year to June 30 have not yet been finalised but its board decided on Monday to write off goodwill relating to an acquisition and the restructuring of Easycall Poland in December 1996.

As at end-December 1996, the carrying value of this goodwill was A$20.7 million and the write-off is based on current assessment of the recoverable amount of the goodwill that existed at the times of each of transactions, Matrix said.
The board also decided to write off business development expenditure in respect of the Indian start-up operations with a carrying value of A$12.7 million as at end-1996.
Each amount is before minority interests and the write-offs will be recorded as abnormal items in the year's results, Matrix said.
The company also announced a number of board changes.
Matrix said Mark Carnegie has been appointed chairman in place of Brian Powers, chairman of Publishing and Broadcasting and chief executive of Consolidated Press Holdings Ltd.
Carnegie is chairman of Singleton Group Ltd and an adviser to Hellman & Friedman.
Powers resigned because he felt his other commitments would not allow him to give to Matrix the time required, Matrix said.
Peter O'Connell, a senior executive of Publishing and Broadcasting, will replace Powers on the board.
Matrix said Telstra Corp executive Charlie Zoi will also join the board, effective September 30.
